confirmed.title: Ban cancel/expiry silently un-pauses a paused user (state reconstructed from quiz_completion, not prev lifecycle)
confirmed.detail: admin_ban_propose (supabase/migrations/20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql) allows proposing a ban on ANY lifecycle except blocked/deleted/pending_ban — so a `paused` user can be moved to pending_ban. But every restore path reconstructs the pre-ban state from quiz_completion only, producing exactly `active` or `onboarding` and structurally never `paused`: (a) the cancel branch here — `const restored = user.quiz_completion === 'completed' ? 'active' : 'onboarding'` (guard.ts:222) passed to admin_ban_cancel, which blindly applies p_restore_state; (b) admin_ban_expire_sweep (same migration) uses `case when quiz_completion='completed' then 'active' else 'onboarding'`. The RPC even returns `prev_lifecycle` from propose but nobody uses it. Net effect: a paused user (self-paused, 'общаюсь с кем-то', hidden from feed, not receiving interests) who gets a ban proposed and then cancelled — or whose proposal auto-expires after 24h — is silently restored to `active`. Per deriveRole/ROLE_PERMISSIONS that flips them to role=verified with be_visible_in_feed + receive_interest. This is a state-machine / data-integrity violation: an admin action (or mere timeout) resurrects a user into the feed against their explicit pause, exposing them to matches they opted out of.
confirmed.repro: User A self-pauses (lifecycle_state='paused', pending_ban_at=null). Superadmin proposes ban (admin_ban_propose → pending_ban, quiz_completion='completed'). Superadmin B cancels (action='cancel'), OR nobody acts and runBanExpirySweep fires after 24h. Restore computes 'active' (quiz completed) → A is now lifecycle_state='active' → role 'verified' → visible in feed and receiving interests despite never resuming.
confirmed.fix: Persist and restore the true pre-ban lifecycle. Capture it at propose time (a dedicated column e.g. pending_ban_prev_lifecycle, or reuse the returned prev_lifecycle) and have both admin_ban_cancel and admin_ban_expire_sweep restore THAT value instead of deriving 'active'/'onboarding' from quiz_completion. Update guard.ts:222 to stop computing `restored` from quiz_completion. At minimum, include 'paused' in the mapping.
confirmed.evidence: admin_ban_propose (migration:75) rejects only lifecycle in ('blocked','deleted','pending_ban'), so a 'paused' user IS eligible → pending_ban. prev_lifecycle is only returned in JSON (migration:100), never persisted — added columns (migration:16-19) are pending_ban_at/by_admin_id/reason, no prev-lifecycle column. admin_ban_cancel (migration:198) blindly applies p_restore_state; guard.ts:222 computes restored = quiz_completion==='completed' ? 'active' : 'onboarding' (never 'paused'). admin_ban_expire_sweep (migration:248) derives 'active'/'onboarding' from quiz_completion. deriveRole (permissions.ts:80,85) maps 'active'+approved → 'verified'; ROLE_PERMISSIONS.verified has be_visible_in_feed (permissions.ts:129) and receive_interest (permissions.ts:131), while ROLE_PERMISSIONS.paused (permissions.ts:143) lacks both. Net: a paused user proposed-then-cancelled (or auto-expired) is resurrected to 'active'/verified, becoming feed-visible and interest-receiving against their pause.
confirmed.verify_note: State-reconstruction is structurally incapable of producing 'paused' since it only branches on quiz_completion. Confirmed data-integrity/state-machine violation. Requires the user to have been 'paused' at propose time; that self-pause path is real (permissions.ts:30 documents self-pause 'общаюсь с кем-то'). Medium severity is appropriate.

confirmed.title: bootstrap burns single-use start-token before the blocked/deleted and bot-step gates, turning a legitimate retry into token_replay
confirmed.detail: claim_start_token consumes (single-uses) the jti at line 106, BEFORE the BOT_OR_LEGACY_STEPS gate (line 120) and the blocked/deleted gate (line 128). If a user is blocked/deleted or still mid-bot-flow, their valid token is already burned when those checks return 403. A legitimate second attempt (e.g. the account gets unblocked, or a transient client retry) then hits claim_start_token → false → 401 token_replay instead of the correct account_blocked / register_required, and the correct one is now permanently unreachable for that token (must re-deep-link from bot). Fail-closed (never grants access), so it is a usability/correctness defect, not a security hole.
confirmed.repro: Blocked user opens mini-app with a fresh valid start_param + valid initData. Bootstrap: verifyStartToken ok, claim_start_token inserts jti (burns it), then line 128 returns account_blocked. User retries same link within TTL → claim_start_token returns false → 401 token_replay (misleading; masks that account is blocked).
confirmed.fix: Move the claim_start_token call to AFTER the BOT_OR_LEGACY_STEPS and blocked/deleted gates, so the token is only consumed once a session is actually about to be issued. Signature verification (verifyStartToken) can stay early; only the stateful single-use claim must be last.
confirmed.evidence: In src/app/api/auth/bootstrap/route.ts, claim_start_token single-uses the jti at line 106-110 and returns 401 token_replay at line 115-117 if already claimed. This runs BEFORE the BOT_OR_LEGACY_STEPS gate (line 120 → 403 register_required) and the blocked/deleted gate (line 128 → 403 account_blocked). So for a blocked/deleted or mid-bot-flow user, a valid token is consumed on the first attempt even though no session is issued; a legitimate retry with the same token within TTL returns token_replay instead of the correct account_blocked/register_required, and the correct error is permanently unreachable for that token. Fail-closed (never grants access), so usability/correctness only, not a security hole.
confirmed.verify_note: Confirmed. Order-of-operations defect exactly as claimed; the stateful single-use claim precedes the two eligibility gates. Low severity is correct since it never over-grants access — only degrades error messaging and forces a re-deep-link from the bot.

confirmed.title: basic/route.ts misroutes all core identity fields (display_name/gender/birth_date/citizenship/country_of_residence/region) into extended jsonb instead of their real columns — publishing and gender-derivation permanently broken
confirmed.detail: The route runs `const { hot, cold } = splitHotCold(parsed.data)` and only writes `hot` (plus `extended`) to user_profiles. splitHotCold (schemas.ts:465-476) is an ALLOWLIST: any key NOT in HOT_COLUMNS goes to `cold`, which the route buries into the `extended` jsonb (lines 32-40). HOT_COLUMNS (schemas.ts:438-462) contains ONLY `district` and `district_visible_public` from the basic payload. The other six fields produced by basicSchema — `display_name, gender, birth_date, citizenship, country_of_residence, region` — are therefore classified as `cold` and written into `extended`, and their real (nullable) columns on user_profiles stay NULL. The inline comment on line 31 (`Cold сегодня пуст (все поля basic — hot)`) is false; it assumed splitHotCold defaults unknown keys to hot, but it defaults them to cold. Columns confirmed to exist and be nullable: display_name/gender/birth_date (init_schema.sql:76-78), citizenship/country_of_residence/region (20260628100000_onboarding_v2_extension.sql:26-28); `extended` is a real jsonb column (20260629000000:57). basic/route.ts is the ONLY writer of these identity columns in the whole codebase, so nothing backfills them later.
confirmed.repro: New user submits POST /api/onboarding/profile/basic with a valid body {display_name:'Ali', gender:'m', birth_date:'2000-01-01', citizenship:'UZ', country_of_residence:'UZ', region:'Toshkent'}. Row upserted as {user_id, extended:{display_name:'Ali', gender:'m', birth_date:'2000-01-01', citizenship:'UZ', country_of_residence:'UZ', region:'Toshkent'}}; columns display_name/gender/birth_date/... remain NULL. Downstream: (1) partner-extended/route.ts:40-47 and looking-for/route.ts:22-29 select `gender` from the column → null → return {error:'no_gender'} 409, hard-blocking the partner step; (2) publish/route.ts:16-37 selects display_name/gender/birth_date/country_of_residence/region from columns → all null → `complete` is falsy → returns {error:'profile_incomplete'} 400 forever, user can never publish; (3) feed/match/progressive-profile readers (recommend.ts, match-of-the-day.ts, admin loaders) read empty display_name/gender. Every newly onboarded user is bricked at the partner step and can never publish.
confirmed.fix: Do not run the basic payload through splitHotCold. Write the identity fields to their columns explicitly, e.g. upsert `{ user_id: user.id, display_name, gender, birth_date, citizenship, country_of_residence, region: region ?? null, district: district ?? null, district_visible_public: district_visible_public ?? false }`. Alternatively (less safe) add display_name, gender, birth_date, citizenship, country_of_residence, region to HOT_COLUMNS — but the explicit upsert is clearer and matches every other profile route. Also correct the misleading comment on lines 30-31.
confirmed.evidence: basic/route.ts:28 runs splitHotCold(parsed.data); line 29 upserts only {user_id, ...hot}; lines 32-40 bury `cold` into `extended` jsonb. splitHotCold (schemas.ts:465-476) is an ALLOWLIST — keys not in HOT_COLUMNS go to `cold` (line 472-473). HOT_COLUMNS (schemas.ts:438-462) from basic payload contains ONLY `district` and `district_visible_public` (lines 457-458). basicSchema (schemas.ts:96-136) also produces display_name, gender, birth_date, citizenship, country_of_residence, region — all classified `cold` → written to `extended`, real columns stay NULL. Comment line 31 ("Cold сегодня пуст") is false. Columns are real & nullable: display_name/gender/birth_date (init_schema:80-82, no NOT NULL), citizenship/country_of_residence/region (20260628100000_onboarding_v2_extension.sql:26-28). Downstream confirmed: looking-for/route.ts:24 selects `gender` column → null → 'no_gender' 409 (line 28-29); publish/route.ts:18 selects display_name/gender/birth_date/country_of_residence/region → all null → `complete` falsy → 'profile_incomplete' 400 (line 38-39). basic/route.ts is the ONLY writer of these identity columns to user_profiles (all other refs are reads: publish, looking-for, partner-extended, admin load-case/load-queue). Nothing backfills them. Every new user is bricked at the partner step and can never publish.
confirmed.verify_note: Fix per report is correct: write identity fields to columns explicitly instead of routing through splitHotCold (or add the 6 fields to HOT_COLUMNS). The upsert cannot fail on NULLs since columns are nullable, so the misroute is silent.

confirmed.title: Case studio page has no moderator scope guard — any moderator can open any case and read passport signed URLs + phone of out-of-scope (incl. closed/approved) users
confirmed.detail: The client card page (src/app/admin/clients/[id]/page.tsx:50) deliberately gates passport PII behind checkInQueueOrSuperPage() so a moderator only sees a user's ПИНФЛ/passport/address/phone while that user is in their active verification queue (verification_status='pending_review' AND lifecycle_state='onboarding'). The case studio page exposes the SAME PII — loadCase() returns 300s signed URLs for passport_image_url + selfie_image_url plus user.phone_number (src/lib/admin/load-case.ts:60-91) — but only calls requireAdmin(); it never calls checkInQueueOrSuperPage / requireInQueueOrSuper. Any authenticated moderator can therefore open /admin/cases/<any-case-id> (IDs are also linked from the global photo/report/moderation surfaces) and view the passport document images and phone of ANY user, including cases already CLOSED (user approved or blocking-rejected) that are entirely outside their queue. This defeats the F-120 data-scope model and is a real moderator-tier IDOR/PII leak given RLS is off. Note the /api/admin/cases/[id]/* mutation RPCs are protected by not_claimed_by_you, but the PII exposure is read-side via the page + signed URLs and is not gated at all.
confirmed.repro: Moderator (role='moderator') with a valid bx_admin cookie GETs /admin/cases/<caseId> for a case whose user is NOT in their queue (e.g. an already-approved user, state='closed'). Page renders CaseStudio with passport_image_url/selfie_image_url signed URLs and the user's phone number — no 403/notFound, no admin_scope_violations row written.
confirmed.fix: In src/app/admin/cases/[id]/page.tsx, after requireAdmin() load the case's user_id and run checkInQueueOrSuperPage(session, userId, 'user_view', ip) (as clients/[id]/page.tsx does); notFound() when it returns {hide:true}. For moderators this restricts case viewing to their active queue while superadmin keeps full access; alternatively gate on the case being open/assigned-to-them rather than the pending_review+onboarding predicate if closed-case review by the deciding moderator is required.
confirmed.evidence: src/app/admin/cases/[id]/page.tsx:16 calls only requireAdmin(); no checkInQueueOrSuperPage/requireInQueueOrSuper anywhere in the file (imports at lines 1-7 confirm). loadCase (src/lib/admin/load-case.ts:66-69,87,90-91) returns 300s signed URLs for passport_image_url+selfie_image_url and user.phone_number. Contrast clients/[id]/page.tsx:50-56 which runs checkInQueueOrSuperPage(session,id,'user_view',ip) then notFound() on {hide}. guard.ts:356-377 shows the scope gate restricts moderators to verification_status='pending_review' AND lifecycle_state='onboarding' (superadmin bypasses). That gate is absent on the case page, so any moderator can GET /admin/cases/<id> for any user incl. closed/approved out-of-queue cases and read passport document images + phone. No admin_scope_violations row written since recordScopeViolationServerPage is never reached.
confirmed.verify_note: Real moderator-tier IDOR/PII read-side leak (RLS off). Mutation RPCs are separately protected by not_claimed_by_you, but PII exposure is purely read-side via page + signed URLs and is ungated.

confirmed.title: admin_claim_verification unconditionally sets state='assigned' on re-claim, regressing data_entry/ready_to_decide cases (state-machine violation)
confirmed.detail: admin_claim_verification only rejects claim when the case is 'closed' or assigned to a DIFFERENT admin. When the case is already assigned to the SAME admin (v_assignee = p_admin_id), it still executes `update verification_cases set state='assigned'` unconditionally. If the case has progressed to 'data_entry' or 'ready_to_decide' (moderator saved a draft / reached the decision step), a second POST to /api/admin/cases/[id]/claim by that same moderator throws the case back to 'assigned'. This is a backwards transition the documented state machine explicitly forbids: ALLOWED['data_entry'] = ['ready_to_decide','in_review','closed'] and ALLOWED['ready_to_decide'] = ['closed','data_entry'] — neither permits →'assigned' (see src/lib/admin/case-state-machine.ts:11-13 and the test at src/lib/admin/case-state-machine.test.ts which asserts data_entry→assigned is not allowed). Draft data is preserved, but the case state (and any downstream queue/SLA logic keyed on state) is silently regressed with no error returned.
confirmed.repro: Moderator claims a case (state→assigned), saves a passport draft (state→data_entry). Then re-POST /api/admin/cases/<id>/claim (reachable directly; the RPC returns ok:true). Case state is now 'assigned' again despite an existing draft — an illegal data_entry→assigned transition.
confirmed.fix: In the v_assignee = p_admin_id branch, make the state change conditional: only set state='assigned' when current state is 'new' (fresh claim); otherwise leave state unchanged (e.g. `set state = case when v_state = 'new' then 'assigned' else v_state end` or early-return ok:true when already assigned to caller without touching state).
confirmed.evidence: admin_claim_verification (20260627100400_admin_case_rpcs.sql:40-53): rejects only v_state='closed' (line 40) and v_assignee<>p_admin_id (line 44). When same admin re-claims, line 49-53 runs `update ... set state='assigned'` unconditionally, returning ok:true (line 57). case-state-machine.ts:11-12: ALLOWED['data_entry']=['ready_to_decide','in_review','closed'] and ALLOWED['ready_to_decide']=['closed','data_entry'] — neither includes 'assigned', so canTransition returns false for these →assigned moves. claim/route.ts POST calls the RPC with no state guard and returns out on ok:true. So re-POST /api/admin/cases/<id>/claim after a draft (state=data_entry) silently regresses state to 'assigned', an illegal backward transition. Draft payload is preserved. NOTE: the claim's detail overstates evidence — case-state-machine.test.ts does NOT contain an explicit data_entry→assigned assertion; the ALLOWED map omission is the real proof.
confirmed.verify_note: Backward state-machine violation, no error returned. Fix: make state change conditional on v_state='new' or early-return when already assigned to caller. Cited test assertion in the claim's detail is not actually present, but the defect itself is confirmed via the ALLOWED map.

confirmed.title: Interest route accepts any active receiver_id, bypassing all matchability filters (self-directed IDOR / integrity hole)
confirmed.detail: The only validation performed on the client-supplied `receiver_id` is `target.lifecycle_state !== "active"` (plus block check). Neither the route nor the `process_interest` RPC (supabase/migrations/20260602170000_process_interest_fix.sql) validates that the receiver is actually a valid match for the sender: no check of gender vs looking_for_gender, no partner-age range check, no `verification_status='approved'`, no `user_profiles.status='published'`. Every one of these is enforced inside `get_recommendations`, but a verified sender can POST an arbitrary receiver_id (obtained anywhere — a link, an old feed, guessing) and create a match_request that skips all of them. Since RLS is disabled and the frontend never surfaces these users, this is a crafted-request integrity bypass: it can create interests toward the wrong gender, out-of-age-range users, or 'shadow' users (lifecycle_state=active but verification ∈ {submitted,pending_review,needs_changes} per src/lib/v2/permissions.ts:27) who have not been verified and are not eligible to appear as candidates. A shadow user could then even receive the interest and, on a reciprocal send, be pushed into a mutual match/chat — entirely outside the vetted matching pool.
confirmed.repro: Verified user A (male, wants female, 25-30) sends POST /api/interest with receiver_id = UUID of user B who is male, or age 45, or still in verification (shadow). target.lifecycle_state is 'active', so the route proceeds; process_interest inserts a match_request with result='sent' and notifies B. B now sees an interest from A despite never being a valid candidate; if B reciprocates, a chat opens.
confirmed.fix: Gate matchability server-side before/inside process_interest. Simplest: add an `exists` check against the same predicates get_recommendations uses (receiver verification_status='approved', profile status='published', mutual gender match, mutual partner-age ranges) — either as a guard query in the route or as an early check inside process_interest returning a new result like 'not_eligible'. At minimum require the receiver to be verified+published and gender/age-compatible with the sender.
confirmed.evidence: src/app/api/interest/route.ts:35-41 selects only (id, telegram_id, lifecycle_state) and gates the receiver solely on lifecycle_state==='active' + areBlocked. process_interest RPC (supabase/migrations/20260602170000_process_interest_fix.sql:22-85 — confirmed the latest of only 2 process_interest migrations, not superseded) applies NONE of the matchability predicates: no gender, no partner-age, no verification_status, no profile status check. Those predicates ARE genuinely enforced in get_recommendations (supabase/migrations/20260626000000_v2_recommendations_viewer_gate.sql:45-53: c.verification_status='approved', cp.status='published', cp.gender=v.looking_for_gender AND v.gender=cp.looking_for_gender, and mutual partner_age_min/max between checks). The send_interest permission gate (src/lib/v2/with-permission.ts:43-84 via requirePermissionForRequest) only validates the SENDER's derived role; it never re-checks the receiver. getCurrentUser (src/lib/auth/current-user.ts) loads only the sender by session, and no middleware.ts exists. Route uses supabaseAdmin() service role, so RLS is bypassed regardless. So a verified sender can POST an arbitrary active receiver_id and process_interest inserts a match_request with result='sent'.
confirmed.verify_note: Confirmed at the CREATION point — a match_request is created toward any active user regardless of gender/age/verification. Two impact tiers: (1) shadow receiver (lifecycle=active, verification in {submitted,pending_review,needs_changes}, per src/lib/v2/permissions.ts:27,87-89) — impact is limited to a stray created request + a 'new_interest' notification; the repro's 'shadow reciprocates -> mutual chat' escalation is NOT reachable because shadow lacks both send_interest AND view_received_interests (permissions.ts:107-119), so shadow can neither reciprocate nor accept. (2) verified-but-incompatible receiver (wrong gender / out-of-age) — B is verified so B sees the interest in received-interests and can ACCEPT (src/app/api/requests/[id]/decision/route.ts:75-87), opening a chat between two non-candidates. Tier (2) is the confirmed path that reaches a real chat. The 'RLS is disabled' premise in the report is not load-bearing (service-role client bypasses RLS anyway).

confirmed.title: Accept path can strand a pair in 'accepted-but-no-chat' with no recovery
confirmed.detail: On accept, the request row is first flipped to status='accepted' via a conditional UPDATE, and only afterward `ensureChat(sender, receiver)` is called. If ensureChat throws (transient DB error / unique-race that its final re-read also misses — it does `throw new Error(...)`), the request is already 'accepted' but no chat exists, and the exception propagates as a 500. There is no recovery path: a subsequent process_interest for the same pair will find no chat (step 3), find no *pending* reverse request to re-mutualize (step 4, because the reverse is now 'accepted', not pending), and hit step 6 `already_sent` — so the pair is permanently stuck accepted with no chat. The accept and the chat creation are not atomic.
confirmed.repro: Receiver accepts a pending request; the UPDATE to status='accepted' commits; ensureChat then fails (DB blip). Request row = accepted, chats has no row. Any retry (re-accept → 'not_pending' 409; re-send interest → 'already_sent') never creates the chat. Users see a match with no conversation and no way forward.
confirmed.fix: Make accept + chat creation atomic, ideally by moving chat creation into a SECURITY-safe RPC that flips status and inserts the chat in one transaction (mirroring process_interest's mutual branch), or create the chat first (idempotent via ensureChat's unique constraint) and only mark 'accepted' after ensureChat succeeds, so a failure leaves the request re-acceptable/pending.
confirmed.evidence: src/app/api/requests/[id]/decision/route.ts:75-87: accept first commits the conditional UPDATE to status='accepted' (lines 75-82), THEN calls ensureChat (line 83). ensureChat (src/lib/matching/chat.ts:22-40) can throw new Error on line 38 (insert error + failed re-read) or line 40, which propagates as a 500. The two steps are not atomic — unlike process_interest's mutual branch which flips status and inserts the chat in one transaction (20260602170000_process_interest_fix.sql:51-58). After the failure the row is 'accepted' with no chat. Natural retries all fail: re-accept -> line 82 !acc?.length -> 'not_pending' 409; sender re-sending same direction -> process_interest step 6 (lines 69-74) matches the accepted row -> 'already_sent'.
confirmed.verify_note: Confirmed, but 'permanently stuck / no recovery' is overstated. A recovery path DOES exist in the reverse direction: if receiver B then sends interest to A, process_interest(sender=B,receiver=A) — step 3 finds no chat, step 4 (lines 47-50) looks for a pending A->B reverse (it's 'accepted' not 'pending' -> miss), step 6 looks for an existing B->A row (none -> miss), so it inserts a fresh B->A pending which A can accept to create the chat. Accurate phrasing: no recovery via the *natural* retry actions (re-accept / same-direction re-send), only via the opposite party initiating. Severity low is right: trigger requires a transient DB fault hitting ensureChat's error+failed-reread branch, not normal input.

confirmed.title: SSE /stream lacks open_chat permission gate — de-verified/rejected/shadow chat members can read live messages the gated routes deny
confirmed.detail: Every other chat route enforces a V2 permission via requirePermissionForRequest: GET messages → "open_chat", POST messages/typing → "send_message", /read → "view_chat_list". These permissions are only granted to roles `verified` and `paused` (see ROLE_PERMISSIONS in src/lib/v2/permissions.ts). The SSE stream route, however, guards ONLY with loadActiveUserApi({ allowPaused: true }), which calls isActiveAccessAllowed (src/lib/auth/active-access.ts) — that returns true for ANY user with lifecycle_state === 'active' (also 'pending_ban', and 'paused' when allowPaused), regardless of verification_status. loadChatRow only checks chat membership + block, not verification. Result: a chat member whose role is `shadow` (lifecycle=active but verification ∈ {submitted, pending_review, needs_changes, not_started}) or `rejected` — e.g. a user who was verified, entered a mutual match + chat, then was moved back to needs_changes / rejected by an admin (a documented de-verification capability) — is denied `open_chat` on GET /api/chats/[id]/messages (403 permission_denied) but can still open GET /api/chats/[id]/stream and receive the exact same live message bodies, read receipts, and typing state over SSE. Since RLS is disabled and authz is per-route, this is a real authorization inconsistency / message-content read hole: the permission matrix is bypassed for the one route that leaks the most (continuous live message stream).
confirmed.repro: 1) Users A and B are mutually matched with an existing chat (chat row + chat_messages). 2) Admin de-verifies A: users.verification_status set to 'needs_changes' or 'rejected' while lifecycle_state stays 'active' → deriveRole(A) = 'shadow' (or 'rejected'). 3) A calls GET /api/chats/{chatId}/messages → 403 { error: 'permission_denied', required: 'open_chat' }. 4) A calls GET /api/chats/{chatId}/stream (same chatId) → 200; A keeps receiving B's new messages, read_through, and typing over SSE. Expected: stream should also 403 like the messages route.
confirmed.fix: Gate the stream route with the same permission as GET messages. Replace `const { user, res } = await loadActiveUserApi({ allowPaused: true }); if (res) return res;` with `const gate = await requirePermissionForRequest("open_chat"); if ("response" in gate) return gate.response; const { user } = gate;` (import requirePermissionForRequest from @/lib/v2/with-permission), matching src/app/api/chats/[id]/messages/route.ts. This makes the read path consistent so shadow/rejected/blocked/deleted roles that lack open_chat cannot subscribe to the live stream.
confirmed.evidence: src/app/api/chats/[id]/stream/route.ts:26 guards only with loadActiveUserApi({ allowPaused: true }), whereas the sibling read routes gate on V2 permissions: messages GET → open_chat (messages/route.ts:25), read → view_chat_list (read/route.ts:14), typing → send_message (typing/route.ts:19). loadActiveUserApi (active-guard.ts:25-35) calls isActiveAccessAllowed (active-access.ts:11-23), which returns true for ANY lifecycle_state==='active' (also pending_ban, and paused when allowPaused) with NO check on verification_status. deriveRole (permissions.ts:70-90) maps lifecycle=active + verification∈{submitted,pending_review,needs_changes,not_started,phone_verified} → 'shadow' and verification='rejected' → 'rejected'. ROLE_PERMISSIONS.shadow (permissions.ts:107-119) and .rejected (161-168) do NOT include open_chat/send_message/view_chat_list. loadChatRow (lib/chat/live.ts:31-42) only checks chat membership + areBlocked, not verification. getLiveState (live.ts:50-87) returns full message bodies, read_through and typing. Therefore a de-verified member (lifecycle stays active, verification moved to needs_changes/rejected) gets 403 permission_denied on GET /messages but 200 on GET /stream and keeps receiving the same live message bodies, read receipts, and typing over SSE. The stream is the one chat read route not covered by the permission matrix.
confirmed.verify_note: Confirmed authorization inconsistency: the SSE stream route is the only chat read/write route that bypasses the V2 permission gate. Fix is to gate GET with requirePermissionForRequest('open_chat') to match messages/route.ts. Severity kept at high (live continuous message-content read hole) rather than critical: RLS is disabled so this is purely a per-route authz gap, and shadow/rejected users lack chat UI entry points, but a de-verified attacker with a known chatId can still directly hit /stream and exfiltrate the peer's ongoing messages.

confirmed.title: promptStep does not handle lifecycle_state 'pending_ban' — user awaiting ban still gets Open-App button
confirmed.detail: promptStep guards only 'blocked', 'active', and 'paused' lifecycle states (lines 277-288). 'pending_ban' is a real lifecycle_state enum value (added in migration 20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql: `alter type lifecycle_state add value 'pending_ban'`) representing a user a moderator has flagged for banning. findByTg only excludes 'deleted' (handlers.ts:89), so a pending_ban user is returned normally. When such a user sends /start (or any message / stale callback), promptStep falls through the lifecycle guards into the onboarding_step switch. A pending_ban user who has completed bot onboarding lands in the `default` case (lines 307-314) and is handed a signed start-token Open-App button — i.e. the bot actively re-admits a user the moderator is in the process of banning. It also sends normal onboarding prompts if their step is mid-flow. The lifecycle guard should treat pending_ban like blocked (or at least withhold the open-app button).
confirmed.repro: Moderator sets user.lifecycle_state='pending_ban' (via admin ban RPC intermediate state). User (onboarding_step past bot steps) taps the bot and sends /start. handleStart -> findByTg returns the user (not 'deleted') -> promptStep: not blocked/active/paused, onboarding_step hits default -> bot replies M.ready with openAppButton containing a valid start-token. User opens the mini-app while pending ban.
confirmed.fix: In promptStep, treat 'pending_ban' the same as 'blocked' (return the blocked/hold message with no open-app button): e.g. `if (user.lifecycle_state === 'blocked' || user.lifecycle_state === 'pending_ban') { await sendMessage(chatId, pick(M.blocked_by_moderator, user.language)); return; }`.
confirmed.evidence: handlers.ts:277-288 promptStep guards only 'blocked','active','paused'; no 'pending_ban' branch. findByTg (handlers.ts:89) excludes only 'deleted', so a pending_ban user is returned. Migration 20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql:12 adds enum 'pending_ban'; admin_ban_propose sets lifecycle_state='pending_ban' (line 85). A pending_ban user past bot onboarding falls to the default case (handlers.ts:307-314) and is handed M.ready + openAppButton with a valid signed start-token (openAppButton -> buildAppWebUrl -> signStartToken, handlers.ts:172-192). Message keys blocked_by_moderator/already_active/ready all exist (messages.ts:116/75). So the bot re-admits a user mid-ban.
confirmed.verify_note: Genuine defect. pending_ban is confirmed a real intermediate ban state; the lifecycle guard omits it, so /start (or a stale callback routed to promptStep at handlers.ts:450) hands a working Open-App web_app button to a user a moderator has flagged for banning. Withholding the button / treating pending_ban like blocked is the correct fix.

confirmed.title: Callback consent handlers guard only on onboarding_step, not lifecycle_state — blocked/pending_ban user can self-advance onboarding_step and verification_status
confirmed.detail: handleCallback's branches (lang/pd/bio) gate solely on user.onboarding_step (e.g. lines 357, 379, 413) and never check user.lifecycle_state. A user whose lifecycle_state is 'blocked' or 'pending_ban' but whose onboarding_step still equals e.g. 'bot_consent_biometric' (blocked mid-onboarding) can click bio:yes and reach the transition() at line 430, which writes onboarding_step='welcome_mission' and verification_status='phone_verified'. The transition_user RPC only blocks patches that change lifecycle_state into ban states (migration 20260619500001) — it does NOT reject onboarding_step/verification_status mutations on an already-blocked user. So a moderated user can mutate their own onboarding_step and verification_status through the bot, and (in the pd branch) record fresh legal consents (recordConsent, line 387/419). This corrupts the verification/lifecycle picture that moderators rely on. Consistent with TGBOT-1, the callback path needs the same lifecycle guard the main-message path is missing.
confirmed.repro: User is blocked while onboarding_step='bot_consent_biometric'. They tap the still-present bio inline keyboard 'bio:yes'. handleCallback: findByTg returns user (not deleted), ns==='bio' and onboarding_step matches, so transition() runs and sets verification_status='phone_verified' + onboarding_step='welcome_mission' on a blocked account — RPC does not reject it.
confirmed.fix: At the top of handleCallback (after findByTg), short-circuit for non-onboarding lifecycle states: if user.lifecycle_state is 'blocked'/'pending_ban'/'active'/'paused', answerCallbackQuery + promptStep(chatId,user) and return, before dispatching on ns. Alternatively add a lifecycle guard inside transition_user for these states.
confirmed.evidence: handleCallback branches gate only on onboarding_step (handlers.ts:357,379,413), never lifecycle_state; findByTg returns any non-deleted user (handlers.ts:89). The bio branch calls transition() (handlers.ts:430) writing onboarding_step='welcome_mission' + verification_status='phone_verified'. TS wrapper transition() (transitions.ts:47-82) reads current user but only guards onboarding_step against ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS (transitions.ts:59-66); no lifecycle check. bot_consent_biometric->welcome_mission IS allowed (types.ts:91), so the guard passes. transition_user RPC (20260619500001_admin_oversight_fixes.sql:196-200) rejects ONLY patches whose TARGET lifecycle_state is 'blocked'/'pending_ban'; it never inspects the user's CURRENT lifecycle_state, so an onboarding_step/verification_status-only patch on an already-blocked/pending_ban user is accepted. The pd branch additionally records fresh consents via recordConsent (handlers.ts:387).
confirmed.verify_note: Confirmed for blocked/pending_ban: such a user, if still on a bot_* onboarding_step with the old inline keyboard present, can self-advance onboarding_step and set verification_status='phone_verified', corrupting the moderator-facing verification/lifecycle picture, and re-record legal consents. Caveat on the proposed fix: 'active'/'paused' named in the fix are not really a corruption vector (they mostly overlap with the intended openApp path), but the core claim about blocked/pending_ban self-advancement holds. The RPC's target-only guard is the load-bearing gap.

confirmed.title: admin_ban_expire_sweep restores wrong lifecycle_state (loses 'paused', prematurely promotes onboarding→active)
confirmed.detail: When a ban proposal expires unconfirmed (24h), admin_ban_expire_sweep restores lifecycle_state by GUESSING from quiz_completion: `case when quiz_completion = 'completed' then 'active' else 'onboarding' end` (lines 37-38). This is not the user's true prior state. admin_ban_propose (20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql:75) accepts ANY state except blocked/deleted/pending_ban — so 'paused' and 'onboarding' users are eligible for a ban proposal. quiz_completion is decoupled from lifecycle_state: /api/onboarding/quiz/complete/route.ts:57 sets quiz_completion='completed' while the user is still in the 'onboarding' lifecycle (step becomes 'attribution', pre-verification). Two concrete corruptions: (1) a 'paused' user whose ban proposal expires is silently switched to 'active' (un-pausing them against their will) or 'onboarding'; 'paused' can never be restored. (2) an 'onboarding' user who finished the quiz (quiz_completion='completed' but not yet verified/active) is promoted straight to 'active', bypassing the verification gate and appearing in matching. admin_ban_propose already captures the true previous state in its return `prev_lifecycle` and could persist it, but the restore path ignores it. The same quiz-based guess is mirrored in the JS callers (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:222 for ban cancel, src/app/api/admin/users/[id]/unban/route.ts:32) — the cancel RPC admin_ban_cancel takes p_restore_state as a param and trusts whatever JS passes — so the defect is systemic, but the sweep RPC is the one place the wrong value is hardcoded in SQL with no external override.
confirmed.repro: User A is in lifecycle 'paused' (self-paused, quiz_completion='completed'). Admin proposes a ban (admin_ban_propose succeeds — paused is eligible). No second admin confirms within TTL. Next /ban POST triggers admin_ban_expire_sweep → row matches (pending_ban_at < cutoff) → restored_state computed as 'active' (quiz completed) → user A is now 'active' instead of 'paused'. A's paused preference is silently lost and they re-enter matching/notifications. Variant: onboarding user B (quiz done, not yet verified) → ban proposal expires → restored to 'active', bypassing verification.
confirmed.fix: Restore the true prior lifecycle_state instead of guessing. Persist the pre-ban state at propose time: add a nullable column (e.g. users.pending_ban_prev_state lifecycle_state) set to v_row.lifecycle_state in admin_ban_propose, and in admin_ban_expire_sweep set lifecycle_state = coalesce(prev_state, <current-guess>). Do the same for admin_ban_cancel (restore from the stored prev state rather than a JS-supplied p_restore_state) and the unban route. At minimum, treat 'paused' explicitly so a paused user is restored to 'paused', and do not promote an onboarding user to 'active' based solely on quiz_completion.
confirmed.evidence: admin_ban_expire_sweep restores lifecycle_state via a quiz_completion guess: `case when quiz_completion = 'completed' then 'active' else 'onboarding' end` (20260619500001_admin_oversight_fixes.sql:37-38; identical original at 20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql:248-249). This value is neither the user's true prior state nor 'paused'-aware. (1) lifecycle_state enum = ('onboarding','active','paused','blocked','deleted') + 'pending_ban' (20260531000000_init_schema.sql:6; 20260619500000:12), so 'paused' is a real distinct state. (2) admin_ban_propose only rejects lifecycle_state IN ('blocked','deleted','pending_ban') (20260619500000_admin_oversight.sql:75), so a 'paused' or 'onboarding' user is eligible for a ban proposal. (3) quiz_completion is decoupled from lifecycle_state: src/app/api/onboarding/quiz/complete/route.ts:55-57 sets {onboarding_step:'attribution', quiz_completion:'completed'} WITHOUT touching lifecycle_state, so an 'onboarding' (pre-verification) user has quiz_completion='completed'. (4) The sweep is live and reachable — runBanExpirySweep() is invoked before every ban action (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:142, RPC call at 107-110). Corruption A: a 'paused' user whose proposal expires (pending_ban_at < cutoff) is restored to 'active' (quiz done) or 'onboarding', never 'paused' — silently un-pausing them and re-entering matching/notifications; the sweep's restored_state has no branch for 'paused'. Corruption B: an 'onboarding' user with quiz_completion='completed' but not yet verified is promoted straight to 'active', bypassing the verification gate. admin_ban_propose already returns the true prev state as `prev_lifecycle` (20260619500000:100) but the caller ignores it (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:168-179 reads only pending_until), and the sweep — running purely in SQL — has no external override. The same quiz-based guess is mirrored in admin_ban_cancel callers (src/lib/admin/guard.ts:222, src/app/api/admin/users/[id]/unban/route.ts:32), so the defect is systemic; the sweep RPC is the one place it is hardcoded in SQL. Confirmed on all links of the chain.
confirmed.verify_note: Severity medium is fair: requires a proposed ban that expires unconfirmed (24h TTL), a specific but realistic path. Impact is data-integrity/consent (un-pausing against user will; verification-gate bypass into matching), not remote exploitation. Fix as proposed: persist v_row.lifecycle_state at propose time (e.g. users.pending_ban_prev_state) and restore coalesce(prev_state, guess) in the sweep and cancel paths; at minimum branch 'paused' explicitly and do not promote onboarding→active from quiz_completion alone.

confirmed.title: containsContact messenger filter bypassed by Russian declension (inflected forms slip through)
confirmed.detail: MESSENGER_RE matches messenger names only as exact whole words via the trailing lookahead `(?![\p{L}\d])`, so any inflected (declined) Russian form with a case suffix is NOT matched. Since containsContact is the core anti-contact-leak control (invariant 1: no pre-match contact exchange) and is enforced on display_name, bio, and every chat message (api/chats/[id]/messages/route.ts:51), this lets users route contact off-platform using the everyday inflected forms Uzbek/Russian speakers actually type. The `_RE` word-boundary approach is correct in intent but the trailing edge is too strict for an agglutinative/inflected language. This is a functional gap in a safety filter, not a dictionary wishlist: entire grammatical cases of already-listed words are unmatched.
confirmed.repro: containsContact returns false for: 'добавь в инсту' (инста→инсту, acc.), 'пиши в телегу' (телега→телегу, acc.), 'я в вотсапе' (вотсап→вотсапе, prep.), 'скинь в вайбере', 'го в дискорде'. All are common ways to say 'add me on <messenger>', so a user sends '@... пиши в телегу' style contact hints (or bare 'я в вотсапе, там номер') and the filter passes them; verified empirically against the exact regexes copied from schemas.ts.
confirmed.fix: Relax the trailing boundary of MESSENGER_RE to tolerate common inflectional suffixes on the listed stems, e.g. allow an optional short letter run after each root before the `(?![\p{L}\d])` boundary (match stems like `инст(?:а|у|е|аграм[а-я]*)`, `телег[ауи]`, `вотсап[а-я]*`, `вайбер[а-я]*`, `дискорд[а-я]*`), or match each stem followed by up to ~3 optional Cyrillic letters: `(...)(?:[а-яё]{0,3})(?![\p{L}\d])`. Add regression cases for инсту/телегу/вотсапе/вайбере/дискорде to mime-check-style tests.
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/profile/schemas.ts:82 MESSENGER_RE uses trailing boundary (?![\p{L}\d]) which requires the messenger stem to end at a non-letter/digit; inflected Russian forms carry a case suffix (инсту/телегу/вотсапе/вайбере/дискорде) so the suffix is another letter and the lookahead fails to match. Empirically verified with the exact regexes copied from schemas.ts: containsContact('добавь в инсту')=false, 'пиши в телегу'=false, 'я в вотсапе'=false, 'скинь в вайбере'=false, 'го в дискорде'=false, while nominative forms ('пиши в инстаграм', 'я в вотсап', 'телега') correctly =true. The filter gates chat messages at src/app/api/chats/[id]/messages/route.ts:52 (if(containsContact(text)) return contact_blocked) and display_name at schemas.ts:106, so inflected messenger hints slip past on both surfaces. PHONE_RE/HANDLE_RE/LINK_RE are independent checks but a bare 'я в вотсапе' with no @handle/digits/link passes all four.
confirmed.verify_note: Genuine gap in the anti-contact-leak messenger dictionary for the agglutinative/inflected RU forms Uzbek/Russian speakers actually type. Real but medium: it leaks a routing hint, not the contact itself — an actual number/@handle typed alongside would still trip PHONE_RE/HANDLE_RE. Suggested fix (relax trailing boundary to tolerate ~3 optional Cyrillic letters per stem, plus regression tests for инсту/телегу/вотсапе/вайбере/дискорде) is sound; scope it to Cyrillic stems to avoid over-matching Latin words.

confirmed.title: Account delete leaves an open verification_case orphaned (ghost case actionable by moderators on an erased user)
confirmed.detail: `erase_user(p_user_id)` anonymizes the user by UPDATE-ing the `users` row (sets `lifecycle_state='deleted'`, nulls telegram_id/phone/name, sets deleted_at) but (a) never resets `verification_status` and (b) never closes/deletes rows in `verification_cases`. Because the users row is UPDATEd rather than DELETEd, the `verification_cases.user_id references users(id) on delete cascade` FK (20260627100100_verification_cases.sql:24) never fires. The account delete route (src/app/api/account/route.ts:45-105) is reachable for `active` and `paused` users (loadActiveUserApi({allowPaused:true})). In the Shadow-Active model a user reaches `lifecycle_state='active'` while `verification_status='pending_review'`, and the VF-1 trigger (20260702000000_vf1_verification_case_trigger.sql) has already created an OPEN verification_case for them. After delete, that open case survives with `state!='closed'`. The moderator queue (src/lib/admin/load-queue.ts:86-113) selects verification_cases filtered ONLY by `state` — no join on `users.lifecycle_state`/`deleted_at` — so the erased user's ghost case still appears in loadUnassignedQueue/loadMyQueue. A moderator can claim and run admin_approve_verification (20260627100400_admin_case_rpcs.sql:120) on it, which has NO lifecycle guard: it inserts passport PII into user_identity, sets verification_status='approved' and avatar_path on a lifecycle='deleted' row, and enqueues a 'verification_approved' Telegram message to a user whose telegram_id was nulled. This corrupts data (approved/identity on a deleted+consent-wiped account, PII re-created after erasure) and inflates the SLA/queue with un-closeable ghost cases.
confirmed.repro: 1) User completes onboarding to lifecycle_state='active' while verification_status='pending_review' (Shadow Active) → VF-1 trigger has created an open verification_case. 2) User POSTs /api/account {action:'delete'} → erase_user runs: users row anonymized to lifecycle='deleted', but verification_status stays 'pending_review' and the open verification_case is untouched (no cascade because row is UPDATEd not DELETEd). 3) Admin opens the queue → loadUnassignedQueue returns the erased user's case (state='new'). 4) Admin claims + approves → admin_approve_verification succeeds with no lifecycle guard: re-inserts user_identity PII, sets verification_status='approved' on the deleted user, enqueues a TG message to a null telegram_id.
confirmed.fix: Close open verification_cases inside erase_user in the same transaction, e.g. add before the users UPDATE: `update verification_cases set state='closed', outcome='user_deleted', decided_at=now() where user_id=p_user_id and state<>'closed';` (add 'user_deleted' outcome or reuse an existing terminal outcome). Also reset verification_status to a terminal/neutral value in the users UPDATE. Defense-in-depth: add a `lifecycle_state not in ('deleted','blocked')` guard to admin_approve_verification / admin_claim_verification, and filter load-queue joins on users.deleted_at IS NULL.
confirmed.evidence: CONFIRMED. erase_user (supabase/migrations/20260620920000_split_window_and_jti_fixes.sql:35-95) UPDATEs the users row (line 77-87: lifecycle_state='deleted', nulls telegram fields, deleted_at=now()) — it never touches verification_status and never touches verification_cases. Because the row is UPDATEd not DELETEd, the verification_cases.user_id `on delete cascade` FK (20260627100100_verification_cases.sql:24) never fires, so any open case survives. An open case exists in the Shadow-Active model: the VF-1 trigger inserts state='new' whenever verification_status enters 'pending_review' (20260702000000_vf1_verification_case_trigger.sql:34, 45-49), and a user reaches lifecycle_state='active' while still pending_review (welcome/route.ts:37 and tutorial/route.ts:88 do ready→active independent of verification; encoded in with-permission.test.ts:65 = {lifecycle_state:'active', verification_status:'pending_review'}). The delete route is reachable for such a user: account/route.ts:18 uses loadActiveUserApi({allowPaused:true}) and isActiveAccessAllowed returns true for 'active'; the only delete guard (account/route.ts:56) blocks reject_category==='blocking', which a clean pending_review case does not hit. After delete, the ghost case still appears in the queue: load-queue.ts loadUnassignedQueue (102-113) filters only assignee_id IS NULL + state='new', and loadMyQueue (86-100) only assignee_id + state<>'closed' — neither joins users.deleted_at/lifecycle_state, and attachRelated (49-84) fetches user rows without filtering deleted ones. A moderator can then claim (admin_claim_verification, 20260627100400_admin_case_rpcs.sql:21-58) and approve (admin_approve_verification, 120-242): the approve RPC checks only case state/assignee/optimistic-lock — NO lifecycle guard — so it re-inserts passport PII into user_identity (line 180-208), sets verification_status='approved' and avatar_path on the deleted user (222-225), and enqueues 'verification_approved' to tg_outbox (237) for a user whose telegram_id was nulled. No later migration closes cases in erase_user or resets verification_status on delete (only 3 erase_user migrations exist; latest is the split-window one). All claimed premises hold; the defect triggers exactly as described.
confirmed.verify_note: Severity high confirmed: PII re-creation on a consent-wiped/erased account plus un-closeable ghost cases inflating the moderation queue/SLA. Fix as claimed: close open verification_cases inside erase_user in the same transaction and reset verification_status; defense-in-depth lifecycle guard on admin_claim/admin_approve and a deleted_at filter in load-queue.
